summary: Benton County summit: a 1915 fire watch, a log lookout from the 1930s, a 1959 tower lost in 1962, a 1963 vista center. A BPA radio station and Forest Service buildings stand there now.

facts.design: 30 x 32 ft log cabin (1933 per register) with an L-4 cab added in the 1940s
facts.status_note: The lookout buildings are gone. The BPA historic report describes a microwave radio station and Forest Service communication buildings at the summit.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Siuslaw National Forest

access.note: Paved road to the Day Use Area, with the summit reached on foot. The road is not maintained in winter, and a visitor guide discourages driving to the summit in the off-season.

visit.trail_note: Summit Trail #1388 (1.6 miles roundtrip) from the Day Use Area, or a gravel access road, per a visitor guide

Tourist vista center with lookout quarters on the top floor; register says used for emergencies in the 1970s and removed before 1980

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kemnow calls Ken Burkholder the first lookout (1937), but the 1915 summer watch by M.P. Burnett came earlier. The story counts the 1915 watch as an early fire watch and the July 1937 station as the first Forest Service lookout.

notes_for_editor: Dates for the first structure conflict across sources: 1933 (register, Kamstra), a July 1937 station opening (Gazette-Times via Kemnow), and 1942 CCC construction (BPA). The register says the 1959 tower was destroyed in 1962; the BPA says the log structure was demolished and replaced by 1959; Kamstra's span is 1933 to 1959. The record's kind 'tower' fits the 1959 structure, but the earliest structure was a log cabin. The Benton County museum page (hbd.bentoncountymuseums.org) timed out and was not read. Trail, road and parking details come from a visitor blog and may be out of date. The BPA summit description may also be dated.
